data.narrative:
Ultima Genomics is a Series C-stage biotech company that has raised $700M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private biotech firms at similar stages, with particular focus on 3 direct Stage C peers: Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression anchoring—applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $700M raised baseline—yields $1.2B. Peer-median analysis across the 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $3.8B, with the range spanning $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, typical for private-stage firms. 

Synthesizing these two methods yields a triangulated range of $1.0B (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.5B. The wide dispersion reflects stage-progression conservatism versus peer-median elevation, driven largely by Colossal's $10.3B outlier valuation. Key uncertainties include revenue traction, clinical/development milestones reached since last funding, and whether Colossal represents sector-wide repricing or an outlier. Further narrowing would require disclosure of recent growth metrics or post-Series C operational progress.
